title: Spatial Patterns of Lipid Composition and Trophic Biomarkers in the Argentine Anchovy (Engraulis anchoita) Across Contrasting Shelf Environments
content:
ABSTRACT

In continental shelf ecosystems, physical-biological coupling between hydrographic structures and bottom-up pathways can generate spatial gradients in prey availability and quality that may influence the lipid quality of small pelagic fish. The income-breeding Engraulis anchoita on the Northern Argentinean Continental Shelf (NACS) fuels reproduction through active feeding and makes tissue lipid quality closely linked to local oceanographic and dietary conditions. This study integrated stomach content and tissue-specific fatty acid (FA) analyses sampled in three zones of the NACS spawning ground under contrasting oceanographic conditions: Río de la Plata salinity front (RP), Mar del Plata shelf waters (MDP), and El Rincón thermohaline front (ER) during austral spring. Diet composition differed markedly among sampling zones, shifting from small euryhaline copepods in RP to almost exclusive consumption of the lipid-rich Calanoides carinatus in ER. These variations were accompanied by differences in tissue FA profiles: ER individuals showed the highest total lipid content, saturated FA, and polyunsaturated FA concentrations, while MDP muscle was dominated by monounsaturated FA, matching Calanidae copepod markers. The omega-3/omega-6 was highest in ER ovaries, indicating selective omega-3 enrichment. The DHA/EPA ratio decreased from RP to ER, reflecting a progressive shift toward diatom-based food webs at lower temperatures, while the EPA/ARA ratio increased from RP to ER in both tissues, suggesting that individuals inhabiting the productive ER frontal system were in a more advanced reproductive condition. Together, these results reveal spatial patterns in tissue lipid quality closely coupled to the physical heterogeneity of the NACS shelf, suggesting a potential bottom-up trophic pathway that may have implications upon anchovy egg viability, larval survival and fish conditions.
